scope: Prevent automatic Chief follow-up from sending operational documents or broad repository queries to the model.
riskAnalysis: Model-selected source is untrusted. Restrict reviewer reads to task evidence paths, bind each transmitted request and count proof, account for both turns, and preserve shutdown and immutable historical receipts.

threatModel.assets: Review grants, provider credentials, exact source evidence, and usage and rejection history.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Owner controller and ledger authorize transport. Model output supplies query data only. The server reconstructs all approved source from the pinned snapshot.
threatModel.abuseCases: Cross-workspace use, replay, secret path requests, changed preimages, usage substitution, and automatic continuation after authority loss.
threatModel.mitigations: Capability and release checks, descriptor path checks, exact counted request proof, compare-and-set admissions, fixed provider endpoint, no retries, and verified revocation.

defects.rootCause: The existing task and one-response stage model could not acquire additional source and resume under the same approval.
defects.detectionGap: The former fixture proved prepared evidence only and could not detect a usage, authority or provenance failure during resume.
defects.regression: Current-source controller fixtures exercise success and HTTP failure with exact request and count ledgers and a final Auditor rejection.
defects.historicalPrevention: Preserve old approval limits and request encodings and explicitly select the successor policy.

rollback: Retain the previous qualified feature alias until the candidate is READY and reviewed. Keep paid execution disabled if qualification fails and preserve all journal records.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Closed schema and private count proof reject malformed provider envelopes and usage.
negativePaths.stale-state: Exact source and release checks reject changed identities and expired state.
negativePaths.concurrency: The existing serial approval and atomic ledger compare prevent parallel or replayed dispatch.
negativePaths.cancellation: Signal and active authority checks precede reads and every provider call.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: The cleanup path closes the attempt, revokes the grant and retains observed usage.
negativePaths.api-outage: A scripted QA follow-up HTTP 503 preserves earlier receipts and prevents all later dispatch.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: The new role path is restricted to the registered policy, active stage and approved evidence files.
negativePaths.spending-limit: The approval bounds all calls and tokens, and the per-stage retained exposure stays below the trial monitoring estimate.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Provider facts are recorded separately for initial and resumed requests; a failed stage cannot complete.

proactiveReview.architecture: Extend the existing controller, provider boundary, broker, and owner console without a second workflow or ledger.
proactiveReview.dependencies: Use existing Node runtime, Redis compare-and-set, source snapshot, and dedicated OpenAI project.
proactiveReview.threats: Prevent untrusted model text from selecting private files, acquiring broad capabilities or driving repository changes.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Reject invalid provider counts, source queries, stale capabilities and unverifiable responses. Retain known usage when the source follow-up fails.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Script a denied read, count outage, provider outage, token mismatch, replay, changed evidence and audited rejection.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: QA and Auditor reviews identified manifest, stale prompt, confidentiality, reserve, and failure evidence gaps. Fixes require exact-diff re-review before hosted activation.
proactiveReview.recovery: Preserve historical approvals and report receipts. Use the existing feature Preview rollback and emergency shutdown.
proactiveReview.readiness: Three local owner-controller tests passed, including private-path denial. Hosted verification remains pending.
